entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Cornelius Scipio Barbatus was a Roman statesman who served as Consul in 328 BC and Dictator in 306 BC.

    As Dictator, he held the comitia to elect new consuls, a crucial responsibility that shaped the Roman Republic's governance.

    His leadership and policies had a lasting impact on the Roman Empire, paving the way for future leaders and influencing the trajectory of Western civilization.

    The legacy of Scipio Barbatus can be seen in the continued relevance of Roman law and governance in modern society, a testament to the enduring influence of ancient Rome.

    "The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall," Scipio Barbatus once said, a quote that continues to inspire leaders and citizens alike.
